name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence in Caucasians compared to African Americans

criteria.description: Presence of ≥20% myeloblasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood
Detection of recurrent genetic abnormalities specific to AML (e.g., t(8;21), inv(16), t(15;17))
Immunophenotypic evidence of myeloid lineage by flow cytometry
Symptoms and signs consistent with bone marrow failure and leukemic infiltration

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: ≥20% myeloblasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood with supporting cytogenetic or immunophenotypic evidence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other acute leukemias and myelodysplastic syndromes.

pathognomonic.notes: Presence of immature myeloid cells in peripheral blood smear
searchTerms: early white blood cells in circulation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bone marrow hypercellularity with myeloblast proliferation
searchTerms: bone marrow with too many immature blasts
excess immature blood cells in marrow

common.symptomName: Anemia-related pallor and dyspnea on exertion
searchTerms: pale skin and shortness of breath

common.symptomName: Thrombocytopenia causing petechiae and mucosal bleeding
searchTerms: low platelets causing small skin bleeds
petechiae and mucosal bleeding from thrombocytopenia
bleeding spots due to low platelet count
recurrent infections due to immune weakness
infections caused by low white blood cells
temperature rise with no infection found

occasional.symptomName: Bone pain due to marrow expansion

searchTerms: lung problems from blood cell buildup

rare.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement with neurological deficits
searchTerms: nerve deficits due to CNS involvement

rare.symptomName: Chloroma (myeloid sarcoma) presenting as extramedullary tumor
searchTerms: tumor outside bone marrow from myeloid cells
green tumor mass from leukemia cells
solid tumor from blood cancer cells

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing myeloblasts with Auer rods
Complete blood count revealing anemia, thrombocytopenia, and leukocytosis or leukopenia
imaging: Chest X-ray may show leukostasis-related infiltrates
CT or MRI for extramedullary involvement (e.g., chloroma)
genetic: Cytogenetic abnormalities such as t(8;21), inv(16), t(15;17), and complex karyotypes
Molecular mutations including FLT3, NPM1, CEBPA
other: Flow cytometry immunophenotyping confirming myeloid lineage
Coagulation studies may reveal disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) in some subtypes

distinguishingFeatures: Predominance of lymphoblasts rather than myeloblasts
Different immunophenotypic markers (e.g., CD19, CD10 positive)
Less than 20% blasts in bone marrow
Dysplastic changes in multiple myeloid lineages

redFlags: Signs of leukostasis such as respiratory distress or neurological deficits
references: Arber DA, et al. The 2016 revision to the World Health Organization classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016.
Döhner H, et al. Diagnosis and management of AML in adults: 2017 ELN recommendations from an international expert panel. Blood. 2017.
